title: Evaluate asymmetric FP8/INT8 KV quant pipelines and calibration automation
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an automated evaluation and calibration pipeline that compares asymmetric FP8 and INT8 quantization for KV cache tensors, quantify latency vs quality trade-offs on long-context generation, and recommend gating thresholds for runtime rollout.

Background: Previous experiments showed mixed signals: INT8 gives better throughput/latency on A100/H100 but occasionally produces degradations in multi-pass attention patterns for long sequences; FP8 has lower dynamic range loss but less consistent speedups depending on kernel support. This ticket centralizes an end-to-end sweep with automated calibration strategies and standardized validation so we can decide whether to enable INT8/FP8 KV in production and under which workload profiles.

Scope:
- Build a calibration harness that supports multiple calibration algorithms (max-abs, per-head histogram/KL, percentile clipping) and both symmetric and asymmetric quant formats.
- Run synthetic and production-sampled workloads at sequence lengths {2k, 8k, 32k} covering streaming and batched inference.
- Measure latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/s), memory footprint, and quality regressions on a representative eval set (response PPL on heldout completions, token-flip rate, and targeted correctness checks for retrieval/QA prompts).
- Produce a decision matrix and suggested runtime gating rules (e.g., route >16k context to FP8, enable INT8 when avg seq < 4k and model variant X).

results_summary:
Preliminary findings from 11/07–11/12 runs: INT8 yields the best latency improvement (p50 down ~15–20%) across both A100 and H100 when continuous batching is present. However, INT8 shows a measurable increase in failure modes for long-context QA and certain attention patterns — token-flip rate increased from baseline 0.6% to 3.4% on the worst workload. FP8 provides milder latency wins (~7–10%) but keeps token-flip rate under 1.1% in the same runs. Hybrid configs (FP8 for the top 4 KV layers, INT8 for remaining) achieve ~12% p50 reduction with token-flip rate at ~1.3%, representing a reasonable compromise.

Calibration algorithm effects: per-head histogram/KL clipping reduced token-flip rate by ~30% vs global max-abs on INT8. Percentile clipping tuned to 99.995th percentile avoided extreme outliers without aggressive clipping that hurts PPL.

Operational metrics: memory footprint with INT8 KV decreased by ~44% vs FP16 baseline; FP8 decreased ~38%. Kernel availability on non-NVIDIA hardware is limited; fallback to FP16 path required in some dedicated nodes.
